comments.comment:
Filed separately from LU-10484, which is the same subtest and the
same shape of failure but was closed "Cannot Reproduce". It
reproduces now, on changes that have nothing to do with each other.

Four failures in 118 runs of sanity-lfsck test_18c on lustre-reviews
between 2026-09-15 and 2026-09-17, all with the identical error and
all on 2026-09-16, on four different hosts and four different
changes:

trevis-153vm38 c7f80ec0-d1b6-4ae2-8e1a-b37c165439e8
trevis-152vm34 c3881a20-edab-4b8f-b351-55db67dd4367
trevis-153vm16 bb982cb3-b5c6-4c99-a56c-46f7a4b50942
onyx-158vm15 eaf41aa8-7dec-4194-a311-424d90933023

(4) Expect 4 fixed on mds1, but got: 7

Sessions are at
https://testing.whamcloud.com/test_sessions/<id>

That every one of them lands on a single day, rather than spreading
across the window, is worth a look on its own: it suggests something
that landed around 2026-09-15 rather than a long-standing flake.
The counts are also stable – always 7 where 4 are expected, never
some other number.

LU-10484 reported the same test expecting 3 and getting 4, so the
overshoot is not new, only its size.

The change I hit this on touches client-side DIO and the obd page
pool only, and three of the four failures are not mine.

Correcting two things in my comment above.

It is not four changes, it is three. Two of the four sessions are
the same patchset, 68928 patch set 1, failing in two different
groups:

c7f80ec0 68928 ps1 dne-part-2, el9.7, ldiskfs
c3881a20 68928 ps1 dne-zfs-part-2, el10.1, ZFS
bb982cb3 68619 ps18 dne-zfs-part-2, el10.1, ZFS
eaf41aa8 68931 ps3 dne-zfs-part-2, el10.1, ZFS

And those two should probably not be counted as evidence at all.
68928 is "LU-19672 osp: batch object destroy over OUT protocol",
which changes how objects are destroyed – which is what this test
counts – and it fails 8 of its 9 enforced groups, sanity-lfsck in
three of them and sanity-quota in three more. Those look like its
own, not a background flake.

I also suggested the one-day clustering pointed at something that
landed around 2026-09-15. That is wrong: master has not moved since
2026-09-06, so there was no landing to blame. The clustering is
just when 68928 was tested.

What survives is smaller but still contradicts "Cannot Reproduce":
two failures on unrelated changes, 68619 and 68931, in roughly 118
runs, with the same error and the same counts as each other.

2026-09-15 0 fail / 12 runs
2026-09-16 4 fail / 49 runs (two of them 68928)
2026-09-17 0 fail / 57 runs

For contrast, test_18e in the same sample fails 2/12, 3/49 and 4/57
across the same three days, which is what an ordinary flake looks
like. 18c does not look like that.

"Hongchao Zhang <hongchao@whamcloud.com>" uploaded a new patch: https://review.whamcloud.com/c/fs/lustre-release/+/69175
Subject: LU-20776 lfsck: do not scan an OST twice for orphans
